findings.location: Table 2 note (df = 196) vs code/main.Rmd m2 and results/main.html
findings.evidence: Table 2 note states 'df = 198 (Manipulation Check), and 196 (Inferred Number of Negative Items)'. The released model m2 <- lm(P24NumNeg~cSelfEsteem * dCond, data = newdata3) has 151 residual df in the stored output ('Residual standard error: 2.409 on 151 degrees of freedom'), i.e. n = 155 complete cases, not 200. The stored coefficients also differ from the table: intercept 3.54802 vs 3.442, condition b 1.42536 vs 1.623, self-esteem b -0.42338 vs -0.448.

findings.location: Table 3, State Self-Esteem column, Self-Esteem row (paper.md line 336)
findings.evidence: Table 3 prints the State Self-Esteem self-esteem coefficient as '.571 (-.544,.032)': the point estimate .571 lies outside its own 95% CI [-.544, .032]. The same CI (-.544, .032) is the one printed for the Manipulation Check self-esteem coefficient in Table 2, so the interval appears to have been copied from Table 2. The authors' stored output (results/main.html, confint(m6)) gives 0.4120894 to 0.7305353 for this coefficient.

The paper reports 'Table 2 NumNeg intercept b' = 3.442 items (Table 2); the authors' own stored output (results/main.html) gives 3.54801601. The gap is small (<5%): it may be run-to-run variation if the stored output came from a different run.

The paper reports 'Table 2 NumNeg condition beta' = 0.293 beta (Table 2); the authors' own stored output (results/main.html) gives 0.282864521. The gap is small (<5%): it may be run-to-run variation if the stored output came from a different run.

The paper reports 'age mean' = 21.0 years (Methods Participants p.2); the authors' own stored output (results/main.html) gives 21.758794. The gap is small (<5%): it may be run-to-run variation if the stored output came from a different run.

'Simonsohn's (2015) 2.5x rule for replication studies (i.e., recruiting 2.5 times more participants than the original) suggests a minimum of 183 participants.': 2.5 x 65 = 162.5, but the stated figure is 183.

'M = 4.83, SD = 1.25) than those in the control condition ( M = 4.24, SD = 1.42; Cohen’s d = .64': the reported d = .64, but the two means and SDs give a standardized difference of about 0.44 (|4.83 - 4.24| / sqrt((1.25^2 + 1.42^2) / 2)).
Paper: average age M = 21.00 (SD = 4.44) years. Stored output stat.desc(newdata) gives Age mean 21.7587940, std.dev 4.4383670 (n = 199). The SD agrees, the mean does not (21.00 vs 21.76).

The paper reports no effect size or equivalence test for the null interaction (only b, SE, beta and 95% CI). The Discussion says the interaction 'may be much smaller than currently estimated' but gives no smallest effect size of interest, so the null cannot be distinguished from an underpowered test.

'We also repeated the study online with 412 participants recruited through MTurk and again found no interaction between self-esteem and condition (all ps > .40).' The materials contain only the lab study: data/EDC_clean2.csv (404 rows = 202 couples), code/main.Rmd (lab models m1-m7) and results/main.html. No MTurk data, code, table or figure is provided, and the online study is not described in the Methods.

Footnote 1: 'times were only recorded for 156 participants [173 in the experimental condition]'. The subgroup count 173 exceeds the total 156. The stored output (results/main.html, mes(73.97, 15.05, 77.57, 36.67, 73, 83)) uses n = 73 experimental + 83 control = 156, so 173 is inconsistent with the authors' own analysis.
